questions.q: What does the DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS setting control?
options: How many days of Time Travel history are kept for an object before it moves to Fail-safe
How many days a user's password remains valid
How long a virtual warehouse stays running before auto-suspending
How many days a share remains active before expiring automatically
questions.explain: DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS is the governed policy for how far back Time Travel can query or restore an object.

questions.q: What are the real DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS limits by edition?
options: Standard Edition: 0 or 1 day only; Enterprise Edition or higher: 0 to 90 days for permanent tables
All editions support 0 to 365 days
Standard Edition: 0 to 30 days; Enterprise Edition: unlimited
Retention is fixed at 1 day on every edition with no way to change it
questions.explain: Standard Edition is capped at 0 or 1 day; only Enterprise Edition and higher can extend retention up to 90 days for permanent tables.

questions.q: What does AT(STATEMENT => '<query_id>') let you do?
options: Query a table's state as of immediately after that specific query ran
Delete all rows a specific query inserted
Grant the same privileges that query's user held
Re-run that exact query against current data
questions.explain: The STATEMENT parameter names a specific query ID, letting you query the table's state tied to that query's execution — useful for pinpointing exactly what changed.

questions.q: What is Fail-safe, and why does this lesson warn against relying on it as a governance control?
options: A 7-day period after Time Travel ends where only Snowflake itself (via support) can recover data — not something you can query or restore yourself
A faster version of Time Travel available only on Business Critical Edition
An automatic backup that restores dropped tables within seconds
A feature that prevents any table from ever being dropped
questions.explain: Fail-safe is a non-queryable, support-only recovery mechanism — your actual, reliable retention policy is the DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS you set, not Fail-safe.

questions.q: What does UNDROP TABLE require to succeed?
options: The table must still be within its Time Travel retention window
The table must have DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS set to 90
The table must be restored to a different schema than it was dropped from
UNDROP works at any time, even years after a table was dropped
questions.explain: UNDROP only works while the dropped object is still inside its Time Travel window — past that, it's no longer recoverable by the customer.
